paper_claim: A declared known truth is not automatically an assignable truth; constrained representations require separate audits of structural realizability, generator accessibility, and recovery.

figures.title: Known truth passes three distinct gates before it can be recovered
figures.question: Where can a simulation-based power study fail before downstream recovery is even evaluated?
panels: A: conceptual flow from declared target to structural realizability, generator accessibility, and recovery
B: observed known-truth recovery rate for continuous-scalar versus nominal-categorical systems in the frozen 722-system programme

figures.title: Categorical failure is an accessibility problem, not a binary state-space ceiling
figures.question: Why do 220 categorical systems fail OU calibration despite having realizable binary states above the target?
panels: A: target rho=0.15 compared with median maximum realizable one-edge rho and median maximum OU-grid rho among the 220 original categorical no-bracket systems
B: mechanism decomposition of the 220 OU no-bracket systems into effect ceiling versus validity collapse

figures.title: Generator choice and state balance independently control truth accessibility
figures.question: How much of the categorical accessibility failure is rescued by changing the generator and then removing the exact state-balance attenuation term?
panels: A: sequential no-bracket rate from latent-OU thresholding to Mk2 and balance-normalized Delta_rank, with the final four-system geometry-HOLD uncertainty shown as a bounded interval
B: paired rescue versus new-failure counts for OU->Mk2 and Mk2-rho->balance-normalized transitions
C: recovery after successful Mk2 assignment: 69 pass versus 37 recovery failures among 106 calibrated systems

design_rules: Use aligned positions and lengths for quantitative comparisons.
Do not use a rainbow palette or rely on color alone.
Show exact denominators and target reference lines.
Show the four-system geometry-HOLD uncertainty as an interval, not an imputed point estimate.
Do not add new scientific estimands while preparing figures.
